export_controls: No new US rule this week. The US now lets NVIDIA sell H200 chips to approved Chinese buyers with a 25% fee, while its top Blackwell chips stay banned. The White House is reportedly drafting a rule to stop China using US AI chips remotely through overseas cloud data centres, but nothing is published yet. China has proposed its own curbs on exporting AI and chip-design technology, expected to be adopted by year end.
chip_security: Nothing material. Background only: Analog Devices confirmed hackers got into its corporate systems (no detail on scope), Advantest confirmed data was stolen in its February ransomware attack, and a ransomware gang claims to have hit onsemi (unconfirmed). None has been reported as affecting chip production.
notes: US chip stocks fell 7.2% (Philadelphia Semiconductor Index) on Fri 30 Oct, the biggest drop since June, after the ASX had closed. Intel fell about 29% on a weak outlook, and AMD, Qualcomm and Arm fell 9 to 11%. NVIDIA, TSMC and Broadcom fell about 5%. SEMI's last price (A$33.78, Fri ASX close) doesn't include this yet, so expect a weak open on Monday.
